item.title: C Language Signed vs Unsigned Integer Comparison Pitfalls Explained
item.description:
“C Language Signed vs Unsigned Integer Comparison Pitfalls Explained”

When performing arithmetic or relational operations between signed and unsigned integer types in the C language, the behavior is governed by strict rules leading to results that often surprise developers. Specifically, what happens when comparing an int (signed) with an unsigned int?

The Root Cause: Usual Arithmetic Conversions

The core issue lies in the C standard’s definition of usual arithmetic conversions (Section 6.3.1.8). When binary operations involve operands of different integral types, they are converted to a “common type.”

item.title: Java Downcasting Rationale: Why Allow Potentially Failing Casts at Compile Time
item.description:
“Java Downcasting Rationale: Why Allow Potentially Failing Casts at Compile Time”

Why does a statically typed language like Java permit code that casts a superclass reference to a subclass type, even when the compiler cannot definitively confirm the cast will succeed at runtime, potentially leading to a ClassCastException? Delving into the mechanisms of polymorphism and type checking reveals the compiler’s approach to these assertions.

The Nature of Downcasting in Statically Typed Languages

When performing a downcast, we are asserting to the compiler that a variable of a more general type actually holds an instance of a more specific, derived type.

item.title: Why Prefer C++ Style Casting Over C-Style Casts in Modern C++ Development
item.description:
“Why Prefer C++ Style Casting Over C-Style Casts in Modern C++ Development”

In C++, the legacy C-style cast, such as (NewType*)expression, merges several distinct conversion operations into a single, often opaque syntax. C++ introduced dedicated casting operators (static_cast, dynamic_cast, reinterpret_cast, const_cast) to make casting intentions explicit, enhancing code safety and readability. Why is this distinction so critical for robust software development?

The Ambiguity of C-Style Casts

The fundamental issue with C-style casts is their hidden nature. They attempt to perform any of the four primary C++ cast types—static_cast, reinterpret_cast, const_cast, or dynamic_cast—without clearly signaling which operation is intended.
